display_name: Withdraw a model capability catalog cell from dispatch
description: Operator ruling rul_2bff72b8 (full lifecycle verbs). Use it to take one catalog cell, or every effort of one model on a runtime, out of dispatch while keeping what the catalog knows about it. Sets acceptance to withdrawn and keeps capability_score, cost_per_task_usd and measured_at; select_dispatch_tier still reads the row but excludes it under its not_accepted count, so a spawn receipt issued for the cell before the withdrawal no longer verifies (selection_receipt_mismatch) and the caller selects again. Required: runtime, model, reason (not blank, at most 512 characters), expected_acceptance (the acceptance the caller read: accepted, pending_crosscheck or crosscheck_conflict) and actor (the session or role making the change). effort is optional; omitted means every effort of the model. The write is a predicated update on the cell id, its acceptance and its updated_at, and every target is checked before any is written, so a cell that moved after it was read is refused with stale_cell_state and nothing is forced. Evidence: one model_capability_refresh_run row with trigger manual, and one acceptance_change observation per cell (source manual_lifecycle, the actor in fetch_method, the reason in raw_excerpt, read back with read_model_capability_history). Reversible with reinstate_model_capability_cell. Effort values outside the known ladder are accepted, so a malformed cell can still be withdrawn.
embedding_description: Retiring a model that was pulled or went bad: stop automated dispatch from choosing it by marking its capability-table row withdrawn, with a written reason and the status the caller last saw, while the row keeps its measured score.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: run_id, runtime, model, acceptance (always withdrawn), cells (per cell: effort, from_acceptance, to_acceptance, the retained capability_score, cost_per_task_usd and measured_at, and the acceptance_change observation_id), reason, actor, reversal (the verb that reopens the cells).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Name each withdrawn cell as model@effort on its runtime, say what acceptance it moved from, and state that its score was kept. Say that select_dispatch_tier no longer serves it and that a selection receipt issued earlier for it will fail verification.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: To undo it, call reinstate_model_capability_cell with expected_acceptance withdrawn. read_model_capability_history shows the acceptance_change observation. A caller holding a selection receipt for a withdrawn cell calls select_dispatch_tier again.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: One manual refresh-run row, one predicated update of each target cell and one acceptance_change observation per cell, all through the state interface. Not retryable: a retry after a transient fault whose write already landed would open a second run row.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: parameter_invalid: runtime is not claude_code or codex; model, effort when given, reason or actor is blank; reason is over 512 characters; expected_acceptance is not a known acceptance or is already withdrawn. cell_not_found: no catalog cell matches the runtime, model and effort. stale_cell_state: a target cell no longer holds expected_acceptance or changed after it was read; nothing was moved by that check. catalog_invalid: a cell row had no updated_at or an observation insert returned no generated id. state_service_unavailable: the state service is not bound.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For stale_cell_state, read the cell again with read_model_capability_catalog (include_unaccepted true), decide again and call with the acceptance you now see. For cell_not_found, check the spelling against the catalog read. For catalog_invalid, read_model_capability_history shows whether the move landed; the run row may be left status running.
